title: The ten main cloud types
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: Every cloud in the sky belongs to one of ten families, and their names are built from just four Latin words. Learn the ten and a glance upward tells you something about the weather on the way.

How to hold it: Build from the parts first: cirrus (curl of hair, high and icy), cumulus (heap), stratus (spread out, a layer) and nimbus (rain cloud), plus alto for the middle level. Then each name is a small sum you can work out, which is far easier than ten separate facts. Chunk by level (three high, three middle, four low), and pair each name with a quick sketch: picture plus words is dual coding. Best of all, step outside and name the clouds you see.
